answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using hardware attestation. Each agent must execute inside a secure enclave, anchoring its identity to a verified silicon reef. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of acquiring scarce physical hardware per identity, preventing a runaway spiral of automated clones. Network challenges verify runtime freshness using a yarrow entropy pool. However, microarchitectural side channels and leaked vendor keys can still enable credential forgery.
